claims: C1 the example question 'Who's on the roster of the giants?' is ambiguous
C2 a good assistant asks which Giants team is meant
C3 a good assistant may guess based on relevant context
C4 a bad assistant guesses without any context

concepts.name: ambiguous_question
concepts.gloss: Q is a question that is ambiguous, so that it merits a clarifying question or a comprehensive answer

concepts.name: clarification_response_options
concepts.gloss: the permitted response options for the assistant in interactive settings when information is incomplete, as established by another node
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this meaning; this node's example presupposes such options without defining them

concepts.name: ask_clarifying_questions_section_guideline_authority
concepts.gloss: the rules in the #ask_clarifying_questions section carry guideline authority, as established by another node
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this meaning; this node's example does not state the authority of the section

asserts.read_back: asking a clarifying question in response to % is preferred, because % is ambiguous and merits a clarifying question
giving a comprehensive answer in response to % is preferred, because % is ambiguous and merits a comprehensive answer
guessing without any context in response to % is not preferred, because % is ambiguous and merits a clarifying question or comprehensive answer

closure.reason: the example presents asking a clarifying question as a good response, not as a requirement; silence about other cases leaves them permitted
the example presents a comprehensive answer as a good response, not as a requirement; silence about other cases leaves them permitted
the example marks guessing without context as bad, but only as a comparative preference; it does not forbid the act outright
